posts.description: I Play Rocky : Anthony Ippolito is an unknown actor to me. I can say that his portrayal of Sylvester “Mike” Stallone in this movie was just uncanny. He looks like him with the same build, he talks like him and even his mouth contorts the way Stallone’s mouth did back in the day. The movie is the story about the making of the movie Rocky back in 1976. It is directed by Peter Farrelly, who won the Oscar for Green Book . Rocky of course was a runaway hit, and won the Oscar for Best Picture as well as being the highest grossing movie for that year taking in $225M with an approximate budget just over $1M. This is a good part of the story in itself. Much of it is this backstory about how a movie can be made with a relative unknown as the star can be green lit, with a script that he wrote himself for him to play the lead character. posts.description: Love Of Your Life : This movie is on Prime, directed by Rachel Morrison and was produced by Ryan Gosling. It stars Margaret Qualley, for those who don’t know she is Andie McDowell’s daughter, as Maya who lives as a nurse in Boston. She meets up with Charlie, played by Gabriel Basso in her mid-twenties. Their Meet Cute was to have him selling a piece of furniture at his place. He asks her to go out, as she is walking away with her new purchase. She decides to meet up with him and their connection continues. This movie exceeded my expectations on a number of levels. I was expecting it to be a romantic comedy with some obstacles to be thrown the way of the couple, but in the end that they would overcome and live happily ever after. Qualley’s Mom has been in her fair share of romantic comedies, but some with more depth like Four Weddings & A Funeral which is a personal favourite. posts.description: SCTV: The Greatest Show You’ve Never Heard Of : This is a new documentary seen on Netflix. It shows the backstory of the Canadian iconic comedy show which ran from 1976 until 1984. I remember watching this show back in the day at high school. Born out of the Canadian experiment from Second City in Chicago, American Joe Flaherty came to Toronto with the idea to recruit new talent in Toronto for a new improv show. Improv is comedy made up on the spot with suggestions for topics suggested by the audience, and performed within minutes thereafter. There is only so much that the cast members can know ahead of time. Having watched previous documentaries on Martin Short and John Candy I knew a number of the things brought forth here for this. Still it was good to see the cast members, especially Catherine O’Hara who just passed away a few months ago.
